responses.response:
I’d first establish what modernization should improve; a tiny CLI does not automatically justify a framework or parser rewrite. Prefer retaining the existing parser unless concrete requirements justify dependency, build-time and compatibility costs.

Proposed scope: argument parsing and output/error handling only. Preserve flags, exit codes and scripting behavior. Use args_os with OsString/PathBuf for non-Unicode paths, without lossy conversion. Keep machine output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr; avoid mandatory color or prompts in pipes. Handle BrokenPipe deliberately without panic/backtrace noise, preserving the CLI’s exit convention. Terminal restoration is not applicable unless terminal modes are introduced.

Edition, MSRV and selected toolchain: independently unknown; no upgrade assumed. Before implementation, inspect authorized manifests and existing conventions.

Proposed verification: cargo check, cargo test, and subprocess checks for exact stdout/stderr/status, non-Unicode path round-tripping, redirected output and an early-closing consumer. Tool availability: unknown; authorization: needed. No commands executed or files changed. Dependency compatibility, current parser behavior and target-platform coverage remain unverified.
